title: Context Fabric shared definitions, contract 1
description: The vocabulary the three tier contracts share. Each tier references this file by relative path, so validation resolves inside the tree and never reaches the network.
$comment: A released contract directory is immutable: changing a shape means creating schemas/<tier>/<n+1>/, never editing <n> in place. Each rule a finding code names carries that code as `x-finding-code`, so a test can map a validator error back to the code without keeping a second copy of the rule.

identifier.title: Identifier
identifier.description: A lowercase-kebab slug. Identifiers reach filenames, view paths, and qualified references, so one that would need quoting or case-folding downstream is rejected here instead.

env_name.title: Environment variable name
env_name.description: The name of an environment variable, in the shape every shell agrees on: upper case, digits, and underscores.

text.title: Text
text.description: A line of prose written for a human reader. Never a credential, never a path that resolves on one machine.

release.title: Release
release.description: The release number of a document. It starts at 1 and rises by one each time the document is released; a reference records the release it was written against.

status.title: Status
status.description: Where a system or interface sits in its life. A retired entry stays in the document rather than disappearing, so a reference to it fails loudly instead of silently.

location.title: Location
location.description: Where another document can be read: url:https://... for anything outside this tree, or file:<path> relative to the tree that owns the referring document. No upward segment is allowed anywhere in the path.

allOf.$comment: The grammar. An absolute path behind the file: prefix is still an absolute path, which is why the first segment may not start with a slash.
No `..` segment anywhere, rather than no net escape. A normalizing rule asks every reviewer to redo the arithmetic, and one of them eventually gets it wrong.

upstream_ref.title: Upstream reference
upstream_ref.description: A reference to another document: which document, which release it was written against, and where to read it. The one shape Bounded Context `extends` and Individual `bindings` both use.

id.description: The id of the referenced document.

release.description: The release of the referenced document this reference was written against.

location.description: Where the referenced document can be read.

maintainer.title: Maintainer
maintainer.description: Who answers for a fact: either an alias standing for a team or role, or the id of an Individual document. Exactly one of the two, because a fact with two owners has none.

alias.description: A team or role alias. Never a person's name: this document is shared and may be public.

individual.description: The id of an Individual document.

organization.title: Organization
organization.description: The organization whose facts this document carries. Nesting is a parent reference only; children are derived when views are generated.

parent.description: The identifier of the organization this one sits inside, when it sits inside one.

maintainer.description: Who answers for this organization's entry.

https_url.title: Transport-safe URL
https_url.description: An HTTPS URL. Plain HTTP is allowed only against a loopback address, which cannot leave the machine and so has no transport to protect.

system_ref.title: Qualified system reference
system_ref.description: A reference to a system in another document, as <document-id>#<system-id>. An unqualified reference resolves today only because one checkout happens to hold one Org document.

secret_reference.title: Secret reference
secret_reference.description: A reference naming where a credential lives, never the credential. Written as op://<vault>/<item>[/<section>]/<field>. The check is a grammar rather than an absence, so that a value nobody checked and a value that passed cannot look alike.

denylist.$comment: Data, not a constraint. Each entry is one shape the contracts reject, with the finding code its match reports and the scope it applies in: `all` runs over every string in every tier, `shared` over Org and Bounded Context only. The derived patterns below are the alternation of the entries carrying each code, in this order, each entry wrapped in (?:...) and joined with |. tests/schemas.test.sh recomposes them from this list and fails if the two differ, so the data and the compiled pattern cannot drift apart.

x-entries.description: The banner line of a private key. Nobody writes one deliberately, which is what makes it worth rejecting on sight.
A forge access token.
A cloud access key id. Half a credential is still a credential.
A chat platform bot or user token.
A signed token with its header and payload, recognizable by the encoding of its two leading segments.
A complete authorization header, value included. Naming the header in prose is fine; carrying its value is not.
A password assigned a value long enough not to be a placeholder. Prose about passwords, and an angle-bracket placeholder, both pass.
The reference form the Individual tier is allowed to use, in a tier that is not. Matched in either casing: a denylist that knows one casing has a documented bypass.
A second vault scheme. The prohibition is on pointing at a credential store from a shared tier, not on one product.
A cloud secret store reference.
A home-relative path spelled as an environment variable, which reads as portable and is not.
A home-relative path.
A path under a user home root. The leading boundary is what keeps a URL path such as /home/index from matching.
A path on a mounted volume, which exists on exactly one machine.
An absolute path under a named filesystem root.
An absolute local path behind a URL scheme. The scheme makes it look like a location and changes nothing.
A drive-lettered path.

finding_keywords.$comment: Data, not a constraint. Which finding code a bare JSON Schema keyword failure reports, for the keywords that have no subschema of their own to annotate. A structural keyword failing is a fault in the DOCUMENT -- a typo, a wrong type, an empty value -- so it is a finding with exit 1. Before these entries existed, all of them reached the validator unmapped and exited 2 as if the checkout were broken, which told an author with a misspelled key that their framework installation was at fault. Each entry carries the phrases the pinned check-jsonschema uses when that keyword fails, so the validator and tests/schemas.test.sh read ONE copy of them; before this, each kept its own, and they had already drifted apart.

x-entries.description: A key the contract requires is absent.
A key the contract does not define at this place -- most often a misspelling.
A value outside the fixed list the contract gives for this field. A rule that names its own code, such as a kind, is more specific and wins.
A value of the wrong type: text where a number belongs, a list where an object does.
An empty value where the contract requires text.
An empty list where the contract requires at least one entry.
A number below the least the contract allows.
messages: is less than the minimum of

x-entries.description: An object with fewer keys than the contract requires.
An object with more keys than the contract allows -- a maintainer is one alias or one individual, not both.

no_secret_value.title: Free of credential shapes
no_secret_value.description: A string carrying no shape the denylist recognizes as a credential. Applies to every string in every tier, the Individual tier included: the tier's permission is to point at a secret, never to hold one.
no_secret_value.$comment: Derived. The pattern is the composition of the scope-`all` denylist entries; tests/schemas.test.sh recomposes it from the data.

no_secret_reference.title: Free of secret references
no_secret_reference.description: A string naming no credential store. Applies to the shared tiers only, which is the framework's one asymmetry: an Individual document is the only document that never travels.
no_secret_reference.$comment: Derived. The composition of the denylist entries carrying SECRET_REFERENCE_FORBIDDEN.

no_local_path.title: Free of machine paths
no_local_path.description: A string carrying no path that resolves on one machine and nowhere else. Shared facts travel between people and repositories, so a machine path in a shared document is wrong for every reader but its author.
no_local_path.$comment: Derived. The composition of the denylist entries carrying LOCAL_PATH_FORBIDDEN.

no_secret_reference_or_local_path.title: Shared-tier prohibition
no_secret_reference_or_local_path.description: The two rules a shared tier adds to the credential denylist every tier carries: no secret reference, and no machine path.
no_secret_reference_or_local_path.$comment: Two constraints rather than one merged alternation, so a failure says which of the two codes it is.

shared_string.title: A string in a shared tier
shared_string.description: Every prohibition that applies to a string in an Org or Bounded Context document.

scan_all_tiers.title: Credential scan
scan_all_tiers.description: Applies the credential denylist to this value and to every value and property name nested anywhere under it.
scan_all_tiers.$comment: Recursive rather than a list of the fields that happen to hold strings today: a field added later is covered without anybody remembering to cover it.

scan_shared_tiers.title: Shared-tier scan
scan_shared_tiers.description: Applies the credential denylist, the secret-reference prohibition, and the machine-path prohibition to this value and to every value and property name nested anywhere under it.
